figs.name: inverting-amplifier-gain-virtual-ground-circuit-diagram
figs.alt: inverting amplifier gain circuit with 10 kilohm Rin, 100 kilohm Rf and virtual ground
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing the inverting op amp from Solved Example 1: Rin 10 kilohm, Rf 100 kilohm, 0.2 V in and minus 2.0 V out.
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 500" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>Inverting amplifier circuit with Rin 10 kilohm and Rf 100 kilohm</title>
<rect width="800" height="500" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Inverting Amplifier: Solved Example 1 Circuit</text>
<polygon points="430,190 430,330 560,260" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#065f46" stroke-width="3"/>
<text x="447" y="232" font-size="26" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">−</text>
<text x="447" y="302" font-size="24" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">+</text>
<circle cx="90" cy="225" r="7" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="90" y="200" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Vin = 0.2 V</text>
<line x1="97" y1="225" x2="150" y2="225" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<polyline points="150,225 171.0,225 179.16666666666666,237 195.5,213 211.83333333333331,237 228.16666666666666,213 244.5,237 260.8333333333333,213 269.0,225 290,225" fill="none" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="3"/>
<text x="220" y="265" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Rin = 10 kΩ</text>
<line x1="290" y1="225" x2="430" y2="225" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<circle cx="340" cy="225" r="6" fill="#1a2b4a"/>
<polyline points="340,225 340,120 420,120" fill="none" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<polyline points="420,120 444.0,120 453.3333333333333,132 472.0,108 490.6666666666667,132 509.33333333333337,108 528.0,132 546.6666666666666,108 556.0,120 580,120" fill="none" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="3"/>
<polyline points="580,120 640,120 640,260" fill="none" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="500" y="92" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Rf = 100 kΩ</text>
<line x1="560" y1="260" x2="700" y2="260" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<circle cx="640" cy="260" r="6" fill="#1a2b4a"/>
<circle cx="707" cy="260" r="7" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<text x="700" y="300" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Vout =</text>
<text x="700" y="324" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">minus 2.0 V</text>
<polyline points="430,295 390,295 390,340" fill="none" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<line x1="372" y1="340" x2="408" y2="340" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="3"/>
<line x1="379" y1="347" x2="401" y2="347" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="3"/>
<line x1="386" y1="354" x2="394" y2="354" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="3"/>
<rect x="170" y="300" width="190" height="60" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="265.0" y="324.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Virtual ground</text>
<text x="265.0" y="347.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">about 0 V</text>
<line x1="300" y1="300" x2="336" y2="232" stroke="#9ca3af" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="4 4"/>

figs.name: inverting-amplifier-gain-rf-rin-selection-flowchart
figs.alt: flowchart to choose Rf and Rin for the right inverting amplifier gain
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing the six steps to choose Rf and Rin, with the output swing check from Solved Example 2 that lowers the gain to minus 4.68.
figs.after_h2: How to Choose Rf and Rin for the Right Inverting Amplifier Gain
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 580" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>Flowchart to choose Rf and Rin for an inverting amplifier</title>
<rect width="800" height="580" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Choosing Rf and Rin: Design Flow</text>
<rect x="50" y="62" width="320" height="58" rx="10" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="210.0" y="85.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">1. Set the gain magnitude</text>
<text x="210.0" y="108.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">from input and output range</text>
<text x="420" y="87" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Example 2: 1.5 V peak in,</text>
<text x="420" y="111" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">plus and minus 12 V supply</text>
<rect x="50" y="142" width="320" height="58" rx="10" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="210.0" y="165.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">2. Pick Rin</text>
<text x="210.0" y="188.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">often 4.7 kΩ to 10 kΩ</text>
<text x="420" y="167" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Rin = 4.7 kΩ</text>
<rect x="50" y="222" width="320" height="58" rx="10" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="210.0" y="245.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">3. Calculate Rf = gain × Rin</text>
<text x="210.0" y="268.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">round to an E96 value</text>
<text x="420" y="247" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">First try Rf = 47 kΩ,</text>
<text x="420" y="271" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">gain minus 10</text>
<line x1="210" y1="120" x2="210" y2="140" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<line x1="210" y1="200" x2="210" y2="220" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<line x1="210" y1="280" x2="210" y2="298" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<polygon points="210,298.0 370.0,342 210,386.0 50.0,342" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="210" y="337.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">4. Peak output</text>
<text x="210" y="358.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">inside swing?</text>
<text x="420" y="330" font-size="18" fill="#b91c1c" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">15 V peak exceeds 10.5 V: No</text>
<text x="420" y="356" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Rf = 22 kΩ gives 7.02 V peak: Yes</text>
<polyline points="50,342 25,342 25,251 48,251" fill="none" stroke="#b91c1c" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="30" y="380" font-size="17" fill="#b91c1c" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">No</text>
<line x1="210" y1="386" x2="210" y2="410" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="222" y="404" font-size="17" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Yes</text>
<rect x="50" y="410" width="320" height="58" rx="10" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="210.0" y="433.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">5. Check bandwidth</text>
<text x="210.0" y="456.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">GBW ÷ (1 + Rf/Rin), keep margin</text>
<text x="420" y="435" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Example 1: 1 MHz ÷ 11</text>
<text x="420" y="459" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">= 90.9 kHz</text>
<line x1="210" y1="468" x2="210" y2="488" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<rect x="50" y="488" width="320" height="58" rx="10" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="210.0" y="511.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">6. Add compensation</text>
<text x="210.0" y="534.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Rin parallel Rf on + input</text>
<text x="420" y="513" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">For bipolar op amps</text>
<text x="420" y="537" font-size="18" fill="#065f46" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">Final gain minus 4.68</text>
</svg>

figs.name: inverting-amplifier-gain-bandwidth-chart
figs.alt: inverting amplifier gain vs bandwidth chart with noise gain for a 1 MHz op amp
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog charting closed loop bandwidth for gains of minus 1 to minus 100 using a 1 MHz GBW op amp, divided by noise gain 1 + Rf/Rin.
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 500" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>Bandwidth of an inverting amplifier for different gains with a 1 MHz GBW op amp</title>
<rect width="800" height="500" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Inverting Gain vs Bandwidth (GBW = 1 MHz)</text>
<text x="40" y="80" font-size="18" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Gain</text>
<text x="160" y="80" font-size="18" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Noise gain</text>
<text x="300" y="80" font-size="18" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Bandwidth</text>
<text x="40" y="128" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Minus 1</text>
<text x="200" y="128" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">2</text>
<rect x="300" y="108" width="330.0" height="30" rx="6" fill="#059669"/>
<text x="640.0" y="130" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">500 kHz</text>
<text x="40" y="184" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Minus 2</text>
<text x="200" y="184" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">3</text>
<rect x="300" y="164" width="219.8" height="30" rx="6" fill="#065f46"/>
<text x="529.78" y="186" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">333 kHz</text>
<text x="40" y="240" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Minus 5</text>
<text x="200" y="240" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">6</text>
<rect x="300" y="220" width="110.2" height="30" rx="6" fill="#059669"/>
<text x="420.22" y="242" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">167 kHz</text>
<text x="40" y="296" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Minus 10</text>
<text x="200" y="296" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">11</text>
<rect x="300" y="276" width="60.0" height="30" rx="6" fill="#065f46"/>
<text x="369.994" y="298" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">90.9 kHz</text>
<text x="40" y="352" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Minus 100</text>
<text x="200" y="352" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">101</text>
<rect x="300" y="332" width="6.5" height="30" rx="6" fill="#059669"/>
<text x="316.534" y="354" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">9.9 kHz</text>
<rect x="40" y="390" width="720" height="90" rx="12" fill="#ecfdf5" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="400" y="425" font-size="20" fill="#065f46" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Bandwidth = GBW ÷ noise gain = GBW ÷ (1 + Rf/Rin)</text>
<text x="400" y="457" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">A unity gain inverter has half the bandwidth of a follower</text>
</svg>
